title: Which of the following plans makes sense to implement prior to performing oral surgery on an anticoagulated patient? (Assume that the anticoagulants stated in the answer are the only anticoagulants that the patient is on and that all of the plans are developed in consultation with patient's physician.)
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Discontinue aspirin and Plavix one day prior to the surgery.
omfs: If the patient's INR is 2.0 or less, discontinue the warfarin for three days prior to the surgery.
midterm: If the patient's INR is 5.3 and emergency surgery is necessary, consider using protamine sulfate to reverse the effects of the warfarin.
column5: A patient on warfarin with a high risk of developing clots is undergoing a procedure with a high risk of bleeding. Check the INR and discontinue the warfarin three days before the procedure. Administer enoxaparin (Lovenox) (low molecular weight heparin) to maintain anticoagulation and discontinue the enoxaprin pre-operatively. Resume the enoxaprin and warfarin following the surgery. Discontinue the enoxaprin when the INR has returned to its therapeutic level.
column6: If the patient is on a target specific anticoagulant, check the INR daily beginning one week before the oral surgery to determine when the medication should be stopped.

title: Which of the following techniques should NOT be utilized for the management of “potential bleeders”?

midterm: Consider doing a “test surgery” - extracting a single tooth rather that several teeth at once to see how the patient responds. Additionally, if a bleeding problem does occur, it would be less critical as it is from a single, smaller area and easier to manage.
column5: Use adjunctive local measures to minimize the potential to bleed.
column6: Patients undergoing dialysis should be treated on the day of their dialysis.

title: All of the following may be useful in minimizing the chances of a patient having a vaso-vagal reaction, EXCEPT:

column6: Ensuring adequate pain control.

title: Which of the following statements is TRUE when comparing diabetic patients to patients without diabetes?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Well-controlled diabetics do not have an increased risk of infection, but if they develop an infection, it is more difficult to control.

title: Which of the following management strategies is NOT a useful strategy for managing diabetic patients?

column5: If possible, surgical treatment should be delayed until a diabetic patient's condition is optimized.
column6: A patient's normal regimen of hypoglycemic medications should be always be strictly adhered to during the pre- and post- operative periods in order to maintain optimal glucose control.

title: Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding HIV+ patients?

title: Which of the following statements related to ORN (osteoradionecrosis) is NOT TRUE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Removal of teeth which have a poor prognosis should be accomplished prior to starting radiation treatment.

midterm: A total radiation treatment dose below 5000 rad (50 Gy) has decreased ORN risk when compared to higher doses. This is significant because 90% of oral malignancies are squamous cell carcinomas which require radiation doses exceeding 6000 rad (60 Gy).
column5: Pre-irradiation extractions should be done in as simple a fashion as possible with minimal bone removal to allow bone remodeling to occur in a natural manner.
column6: HBO (hyperbaric oxygen) may be a useful adjunctive therapy when it is necessary to perform oral surgery in patients who are at risk for ORN (osteoradionecrosis) due to radiation to the head and neck region.

title: Which of the following statements regarding a patient's heart rate is TRUE?
